sempra-ienova-gasoducto-loma-de-bacum.whole: The Guaymas-El Oro section is 330 km long with capacity for 510 million cubic feet of gas a day, by IEnova's and Mexico's energy ministry's figures (via Global Energy Monitor). Construction finished in May 2017 and the line ran commercially for about three months before service was cut in August 2017 (Global Energy Monitor). Reuters reported in July 2022 that it had been inoperable since late 2017 and that Sempra and the state power company CFE had agreed a framework to restore it. Citing Sempra's February 2026 annual report, Zeta Tijuana reported in March 2026 that the interruption since 2017 continued and that CFE would repay rerouting costs if the line is back in service by July 2029; in May 2026 a Sinaloa official said a new route around the disputed stretch was being worked on (Luz Noticias). No report of it returning to service was found.

drc-2002-mining-code.whole: Copper output rose from an estimated 34,000 tonnes in 2002 to 1,030,129 tonnes in 2014, and cobalt from 14,500 to 62,000 tonnes, by US Geological Survey figures; in 2016 the country mined 58% of the world's cobalt, and copper (56%), cobalt (21%) and gold (13%) made up most of its US$10 billion exports (USGS). State miner Gécamines said in 2018 that the code did not let the country fully benefit, and the Carter Center reported almost US$750 million of partnership payments to Gécamines in 2011-2014 missing from its accounts (MINING.COM). A 2018 revision raised base-metal royalties from 2% to 3.5%, the state share from 5% to 10% and added a 50% super-profits tax (Herbert Smith Freehills).

arun-iii-hill-route-compensation.whole: The dam the road was built for was not built under the credit: World Bank president James Wolfensohn cancelled Arun III on 1 August 1995, citing doubts about Nepal's capacity to manage it, difficulty winning public backing for tariff changes, and difficulty paying for a US$30-40 million overrun (Kathmandu Post, 2022). Nepali Times reported in 2004 that the access road from Dharan to the dam site cost Rs 50 million per km against Rs 6 million for other Nepali roads, and that the road from Hile had only reached Leguwa; former finance minister Ram Sharan Mahat said about US$400 million in committed grants and loans was written off. India's SJVN is now building a 900 MW Arun-3 plant; as of 4 November 2026 it was still under construction with no generation reported (Indian Masterminds).

These are planned capacities, not results. allAfrica reported in February 2026 that the 2025-26 season opened with a target of more than 120,000 tonnes from Sukala and N-Sukala together, about 34% of national demand, leaving about 66% to imports. No actual production figures for N-Sukala alone, and no independent check of its output, were found.

nandigram-salim-sez-firing.whole: The chemical hub was never built. On 29 March 2007 Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee announced it would be scrapped at Nandigram and relocated, possibly to Haldia (PTI, via Business Standard). PTI reported in 2021 that the planned hub covered 10,000 acres and that no industrialist had come to Nandigram since, with most families earning no more than Rs 6,000 a month. The land later allotted at Nayachar to Universal Success Enterprises, which had a stake in the Salim hub, was for Rs 26,000 crore of projects that the state said in 2016 it would take back (Business Standard).

southern-cardamom-redd-chong.whole: Verra issued more than 27 million credits to the project between 2018 and 2023 (Human Rights Watch). A registry disclosure by BMO, a credit intermediary, gives an area of 445,339 hectares (Carbon Herald says 450,000), an estimated 3.87 million tonnes of emission reductions a year and about 12 million tonnes avoided in the first monitoring period; these are the developer's own estimates. In September 2024 Verra lifted its hold, saying Wildlife Alliance had taken steps to address the alleged harms; HRW's lead author called the review deeply insufficient and said Verra interviewed no victims (Carbon Herald). No independent measure of deforestation avoided was found.

No independent figures on output or revenue were found.

perenco-muanda-oil.whole: Perenco, which Human Rights Watch describes as the DRC's only producing oil operator, has historically reported about 20,000 to 25,000 barrels a day, its own figure (Bankable, 2026). The DRC's 2024 EITI report found a 972,000-barrel gap between sources for 2022 production and a gap of more than US$200 million between declared exports and partners' recorded imports (Bankable). Perenco told Mongabay in 2023 that it supplies 2 MW of electricity to Muanda directly and 3 MW more through gas-to-power.

wilmar-php1-kapa-pasaman.whole: Mongabay Indonesia reported in 2015 that PT PHP1 holds an HGU of about 1,600 hectares (2004) and runs a mill with yearly capacity of 135,250 tonnes of fruit bunches and 28,600 tonnes of crude palm oil, about 75% sold abroad; no independent check of these figures was found. It reported that the company handed over 353 hectares of smallholder (plasma) plots in 2004 and 344 hectares in 2009; the company says it has handed over all the plasma owed, while the community is not satisfied with the area handed over. In February 2017 the RSPO complaints panel ruled PT PHP1 had not followed proper process in acquiring Kapa land (Eco-Business).
